facts_found: Identity verification using standard verification procedures is required before an agent accesses or acts on a customer's account/transaction data. [doc_credit_cards_credit_card_account_logistics_002]

Cash back is calculated on the posted amount of each eligible purchase (net of returns/credits) multiplied by the card's applicable rate; e.g., 1.0% on Bronze Rewards Card, 2.5% on Business Gold operations spend, 4.0%/1.5% on Business Platinum, 5.0% on Diamond Elite, 10.0% on Platinum Rewards. [doc_credit_cards_bronze_rewards_card_002]

Bonus/enhanced rates are determined by the merchant category code assigned by the merchant's payment processor, so a miscoded merchant can produce a lower-than-expected reward rate. [doc_business_credit_cards_business_gold_rewards_card_002]

Rewards accrue when transactions post and clear; returns or credits reduce/reverse previously earned rewards on a per-transaction basis in the period the adjustment posts. [doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_002]
Ineligible transactions: cash advances, balance transfers, fees, interest, and other cash-equivalent transactions do not earn cash back. [doc_credit_cards_platinum_rewards_card_002]
Disputed transactions do not earn rewards until the dispute is resolved and the transaction posts. [doc_credit_cards_bronze_rewards_card_002]

All credit card rewards are stored in the transaction database as 'points' (legacy migration), including cash back cards; 1 point = $0.01 when redeemed as a statement credit or checking-account credit (250 points = $2.50 = 2.5% on a $100 purchase). [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

Rewards points are always rounded down (floored) to the nearest whole point; e.g., $99.99 at 2.5% = 249.975 points awarded as 249 points. This applies to all card types and reward categories. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007]

Signs of a cash back error: a purchase that should have earned bonus cash back received only the standard rate; a bonus-category purchase that did not receive the higher rate; cash back lower than the customer's calculation from card rates; a qualifying purchase with no rewards; suspected merchant miscategorization. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

Customer service investigates by looking into the specific transaction, verifying the merchant category, checking the applicable reward rates for the card, and determining whether an adjustment is needed. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

Helpful intake information for a cash back review: transaction date, merchant name and purchase amount, cash back received vs. expected, and any receipts/documentation. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

To report a discrepancy the customer must run the user tool submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id: str, transaction_id: str) with their own user_id and the specific transaction_id; this applies to all credit card transactions. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

Agent notes for dispute submission: confirm the customer has the correct transaction_id before submitting, do not collect sensitive card details, and advise that supporting context (category or promotion expectations) may be requested later during review. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

Corrections are applied only after a cash back dispute is resolved and approved; the agent looks up the user's resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database to obtain the transaction_id values needing adjustment. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

The agent must unlock update_transaction_rewards_3847 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool and then invoke it with call_discoverable_agent_tool, passing transaction_id and new_rewards_earned as a string formatted 'X points' with a whole-number point value. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

The agent must independently recalculate correct rewards from card type, transaction category and applicable promotions and must NOT rely on any expected_rewards field in the dispute record. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

After the rewards update tool call completes, the agent confirms the change in credit_card_transaction_history and retains calculation notes in the internal case record for auditability. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

A separate mechanism, apply_statement_credit_8472 (unlocked then called via call_discoverable_agent_tool), applies dollar statement credits to a credit card account and supports reason 'error_correction' / 'dispute_resolution'; the credit_card_account_id is obtained via get_credit_card_accounts_by_user. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_017]

A formal transaction dispute (unauthorized charge, billing error, etc.) is a different process filed by the agent with file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 and is not the cash back rewards discrepancy path. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_014]

Cash back card types listed in the rewards-representation policy: Bronze Rewards, Silver Rewards, Gold Rewards, Platinum Rewards, Diamond Elite, Crypto-Cash Back, Business Bronze Rewards, Business Silver Rewards, Green Rewards, Silver Zoom, Business Gold Rewards, Business Platinum Rewards (EcoCard is the only true points-based card). [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

facts_found: EcoCard is the only true points-based card; it earns 'sustainability points' (5 points per dollar on green purchases, 1 point per dollar on other purchases) that redeem at $0.01 per point as statement or checking-account credit. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

EcoCard earning rates: green purchases earn 5.00 sustainability points per dollar at qualifying green merchants/categories; other purchases earn 1.00 sustainability point per dollar. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]

Green (5x) criteria generally include public transportation passes/fares, electric vehicle charging, renewable energy subscriptions/providers, certified sustainable retailers and eco-labeled products, and local bike share/micromobility services. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard maintains a network of approximately 3 certified green merchant partners whose purchases are automatically recognized as green; eligibility is shown via a green badge in the merchant directory and a green indicator on receipts/statements. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Green-rate edge cases: marketplaces/delivery platforms processing through non-green parent entities may not qualify; mixed carts at non-partner merchants may not qualify if item-level green data is unavailable; gift cards and cash equivalents typically do not qualify as green purchases. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Excluded from the 5x sustainability rate (earn 1x instead): Target, Walmart, Amazon (all channels, including eco-labeled items and Amazon-marketplace orders processed by Amazon), and ThredUp. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

EV charging only earns the 5x green rate on the 3 certified partner networks Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo; charging at any other network earns the standard 1x rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

All credit card rewards points are rounded down (floored) to the nearest whole number; e.g., $99.99 at 2.5% = 249.975 points awarded as 249. This applies across all card types and reward categories. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007]
If an EcoCard transaction is returned or refunded, the corresponding points are reversed at the original earn rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]

EcoCard redemption requires at least 3,000 points available and is valued at $0.01 per point; only posted (not pending) points count and point reversals must settle first. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_005]

EcoCard New Customer Promo: earn 2,000 sustainability points by spending at least $5,000 in eligible purchases within the first 1 month of account opening; offer window runs 2025-08-01 through 2025-12-15; returns/chargebacks/disputes reduce qualifying spend and balance transfers/cash equivalents/fees do not count. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_009]

EcoCard application terms: annual fee $50.00, purchase APR 19.99%, foreign transaction fee 1.0%, late payment fee $32.50, initial credit lines typically $5,000 to $50,000; sign-up bonus described as 2,000 sustainability points for $5,000 in eligible purchases in the first month. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_001]

open_questions: No EcoCard-specific article explicitly enumerates transaction types that earn ZERO points at all (e.g., cash advances, fees, interest, balance transfers); the only EcoCard statements on non-earning items are promo-threshold exclusions (balance transfers, cash equivalents, fees) and the green-rate edge cases (gift cards/cash equivalents).

The complete named list of the ~3 certified green merchant partners is not provided (only the 3 EV-charging networks are named); partner lists are described as evolving and must be checked in the in-app directory.
No documented cap/limit on bonus (5x) sustainability points per transaction, per period, or per year was found.
No documented time window or filing deadline for EcoCard rewards discrepancies was found (consistent with earlier gap).

facts_found: In the cash-back discrepancy process, Rho-Bank's customer service team investigates by looking into the specific transaction, verifying the merchant category, checking the applicable reward rates for the card, and determining whether an adjustment is needed — the verification is performed by the bank, not supplied by the customer. Customer-side requirements for a rewards review are framed as 'helpful to have ready' (transaction date, merchant name and amount, received vs expected rewards, and any receipts or documentation you have) — not as mandatory evidence for filing. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_021]

The cash-back dispute is submitted by the customer running submit_cash_back_dispute_0589(user_id, transaction_id); only those two identifiers are required, and agents must not collect sensitive card details. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]

Agents are to advise the customer that supporting context (e.g., category or promotion expectations) may be requested later during review, but the submission itself is initiated with the tool — evidence is not a precondition to start the review. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003]
EcoCard guidance: if you believe a purchase should qualify as green, contact support with your receipt and merchant details for review. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard eligibility markers are customer-side checks: look for a green badge in the merchant directory before you pay, and eligible transactions 'may display' a green indicator on receipts and statements (permissive, not guaranteed). [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard advises keeping receipts for any purchases you believe should be recognized as eco-friendly if you need to request a review, and confirming the seller of record is the certified partner rather than a third-party marketplace. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_007]

The in-app merchant directory filtered for certified green partners is the customer's tool for confirming partner status; partner lists can evolve, so the directory should be re-checked, and unlisted eco merchants can be suggested through the directory's feedback option. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_007]
EcoCard says saving receipts helps in resolving earn-rate disputes, and that mixed green/non-green carts at a non-partner merchant may all earn the non-green rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]

After a cash-back dispute is resolved and approved, the agent recalculates correct rewards independently from card type, transaction category and applicable promotions (not the dispute record's expected_rewards) and applies them via update_transaction_rewards_3847. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004]

[doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002]

facts_found: EcoCard is the only true points-based card; it earns 'sustainability points' (5 points per dollar on green purchases, 1 point per dollar on other purchases) that redeem at $0.01 per point as statement or checking-account credit. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_006]

EcoCard earning rates: green purchases earn 5.00 sustainability points per dollar at qualifying green merchants/categories; other purchases earn 1.00 sustainability point per dollar. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]

Green (5x) criteria generally include public transportation passes/fares, electric vehicle charging, renewable energy subscriptions/providers, certified sustainable retailers and eco-labeled products, and local bike share/micromobility services. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

EcoCard maintains a network of approximately 3 certified green merchant partners whose purchases are automatically recognized as green; eligibility is shown via a green badge in the merchant directory and a green indicator on receipts/statements. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Green-rate edge cases: marketplaces/delivery platforms processing through non-green parent entities may not qualify; mixed carts at non-partner merchants may not qualify if item-level green data is unavailable; gift cards and cash equivalents typically do not qualify as green purchases. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_003]

Excluded from the 5x sustainability rate (earn 1x instead): Target, Walmart, Amazon (all channels, including eco-labeled items and Amazon-marketplace orders processed by Amazon), and ThredUp. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

EV charging only earns the 5x green rate on the 3 certified partner networks Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint, or EVgo; charging at any other network earns the standard 1x rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_004]

All credit card rewards points are rounded down (floored) to the nearest whole number; e.g., $99.99 at 2.5% = 249.975 points awarded as 249. This applies across all card types and reward categories. [doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007]
If an EcoCard transaction is returned or refunded, the corresponding points are reversed at the original earn rate. [doc_credit_cards_ecocard_002]
